items.headline: Three Sunday polls: Kan has Yashar 23 and Likud 21; i24NEWS has Likud 25; Channel 14 has Netanyahu's bloc at exactly 61
items.lead: Three seat polls published on Sunday evening, 18 October, nine days before the vote, point in different directions.
items.text: Three seat polls published on Sunday evening, 18 October, nine days before the vote, point in different directions. Kan News (Kantar, Dudu Hasid; 554 respondents, margin of error 4.2 points) gives Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar 23 seats and Likud 21, each up one from last week; Bennett's Beyachad 12; the Democrats 9, their highest since early September; Otzma Yehudit, Shas, Yisrael Beytenu and the Joint List (Hadash–Ta'al–Balad) 8 each; Religious Zionism 7, up from 5; United Torah Judaism 7; Ra'am 5; and the Hendel–Zelekha Reservists 4. Ofer Winter's Amcha Yisrael falls below the threshold at 3.1 percent. The Eisenkot bloc has 52 seats and the Netanyahu bloc 51, with the Arab parties at 13. Eisenkot leads Netanyahu 43 to 35 percent as more suitable for prime minister (Netanyahu had 38 a week earlier); Netanyahu leads Bennett 38 to 34. Thirty percent of respondents said they had not yet decided how to vote. An i24NEWS poll by Direct Polls (Tzuriel Sharon; 525 respondents, margin of error 4.2 points) has Likud at 25, down two; Yashar 21; Beyachad 13; Otzma Yehudit 10, its first double-digit result in this series; the Democrats 9; United Torah Judaism, Shas and the Joint List 8 each; and Yisrael Beytenu, Religious Zionism and Ra'am 6 each. The coalition parties total 57, the Zionist opposition 49 and the Arab parties 14; Winter (2.9 percent) and the Reservists (2.4 percent) are out. A Channel 14 poll by Next Data (559 respondents, fielded 18 October) keeps Likud at 29 and raises Yashar from 20 to 22; Shas and Beyachad have 10 each; the Democrats and United Torah Judaism 8 each; Religious Zionism, Otzma Yehudit and the Joint List 7 each; Yisrael Beytenu and Ra'am 6 each. It puts the right-wing bloc at exactly 61, down one from Wednesday, and narrows Netanyahu's head-to-head lead over Eisenkot to 51–49. On Polymarket, Eisenkot stood at about 46 percent early on Monday, Israel time, Netanyahu at about 29.5 and Bennett at about 12.5 (about $48.5 million traded), against about 47, 32 and 14 on Sunday evening.

items.headline: Netanyahu presents a new security doctrine: 'The regime must fall, and I will bring it down'; Eisenkot calls it 'two hollow pages'
items.lead: On Sunday Netanyahu held a two-hour security briefing for Israeli reporters at his Jerusalem office, his first such in-person briefing since 7 October 2023; several outlets boycotted it (Times of Israel).
items.text: On Sunday Netanyahu held a two-hour security briefing for Israeli reporters at his Jerusalem office, his first such in-person briefing since 7 October 2023; several outlets boycotted it (Times of Israel). He presented an updated national security doctrine that puts preemptive offensive action ahead of containment, said bringing down Iran's regime remains the main goal ('The regime must fall, and I will bring it down'), claimed that about 90 percent of the work against Israel's enemies is done, and said Israel will act alone against Iran if necessary. He said he would put about NIS 450 billion into defense over the next decade, including more domestic weapons production (Ynet; Times of Israel). He warned that 'in two years' a U.S. president 'very hostile to Israel' could take office, and said Israel must build alliances with India and Latin America. On the next coalition he rejected a unity government with his opponents, said he wants a 'broad national government' that keeps his current partners, including Ben-Gvir's party, and said he would pass a Haredi enlistment law after the election. He called the international reaction to recent settler attacks 'a huge exaggeration' while saying the rioters cause Israel 'enormous damage.' Eisenkot answered that the doctrine was 'two hollow pages, full of slogans that have nothing whatsoever to do with a security doctrine' and an attempt to frighten voters (Ynet).

items.headline: Former chief rabbi Yitzhak Yosef rules it forbidden to vote for Otzma Yehudit; IDF weighs a leave freeze on election day
items.lead: Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef, the former Sephardi chief rabbi and a member of Shas's Council of Torah Sages, published a letter on Sunday ruling that it is forbidden under Jewish law to vote for Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit, because Ben-Gvir goes up to the Temple Mount and encourages others to do so; he wrote that whoever votes for the party carries the sin (Arutz 7; Times of Israel).
items.text: Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef, the former Sephardi chief rabbi and a member of Shas's Council of Torah Sages, published a letter on Sunday ruling that it is forbidden under Jewish law to vote for Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit, because Ben-Gvir goes up to the Temple Mount and encourages others to do so; he wrote that whoever votes for the party carries the sin (Arutz 7; Times of Israel). Shas and Otzma compete for some of the same religious right-wing voters; Otzma had between 7 and 10 seats in Sunday's three polls. Channel 12 (N12) reported on Sunday that Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir had decided to cancel leave for soldiers on election day, 27 October, because of concern about attacks meant to influence the vote. The IDF's own statement said an alert order had placed additional ground forces on standby and that a decision on leave 'has not yet been finalized' and would be made later this week (Times of Israel). Responding to Trump's endorsement of Netanyahu, Eisenkot said that 'Israel's citizens are the only ones who will decide,' told Channel 12 that he had asked in meetings that there be no intervention in Israel's election, and said the leader of the largest party should be 'the natural candidate' for prime minister. Trump told Axios, as quoted by the Times of Israel, 'I was always going to do that. I just didn't want to do it too soon.'

sources.name: The Times of Israel (live blog, 18 October)

items.headline: Before the Tampa talks: Lebanon's demands, Netanyahu's verdict on the army's pilot zones, and a Hezbollah defense of arms transfers
items.lead: The US–Lebanon–Israel military meeting at US Central Command in Tampa is set for Tuesday, 20 October.
items.text: The US–Lebanon–Israel military meeting at US Central Command in Tampa is set for Tuesday, 20 October. According to Arab media cited by Israel Hayom, Lebanon's delegation has been told to seek a halt to Israeli air strikes and bulldozer work in border villages, a timetable for Israeli withdrawal, wider Lebanese army deployment along the border, procedures for withdrawal and handover, and a mechanism for handling violations; Beirut also wants its army to be the only body that carries out security checks and disarmament. Netanyahu told reporters on Sunday that Israel had let the Lebanese army show it could clear Hezbollah infrastructure in two pilot areas, but that it had 'not demonstrated sufficient capabilities,' and that Israel would do the job itself if the army cannot (Times of Israel; not found in a second report). Hezbollah MP Hassan Fadlallah, speaking in Tibnin on Sunday, defended the group's right to move weapons to the front: 'How will it fight this enemy? Are we supposed to fight with bags of potatoes?' (L'Orient Today; not independently confirmed). After Army Radio reported on Sunday that the IDF allows olive picking inside its security strip, residents of the Arqoub villages refused to go to their groves near Kfar Shouba on the IDF's terms, which, according to Lebanese reports, included handing over phones and ID cards, a limit of 100 people and 25 vehicles, and no Lebanese army or UNIFIL escort; the head of the Kfar Shouba municipality said an Israeli patrol then ordered farmers in another area to leave (L'Orient Today; Lebanon Times). No IDF account of these conditions was found.

items.headline: EUSM Lebanon watch: Ireland's government moves to take part; still no Israeli reaction
items.lead: Ireland's government has said it wants to contribute to the EU Support Mission in Lebanon.
items.text: Ireland's government has said it wants to contribute to the EU Support Mission in Lebanon. Foreign Affairs and Defence Minister Helen McEntee said on 12 October that the coalition wants Ireland to 'participate fully in any European mission to Lebanon' and would bring forward legislation to remove the 'Triple Lock' requirement of UN Security Council approval for sending more than 12 Irish troops abroad (Highland Radio). RTÉ reported on 18 October that the bill is now before the Oireachtas, that opposition parties strongly oppose it as a threat to Irish neutrality, and that the exact nature of the mission's military component is still unclear. Ireland's last UNIFIL contingent, about 300 soldiers, deploys next month, and McEntee has said Irish forces will be out of south Lebanon entirely by Easter. No decision to send Irish personnel to the EU mission has been taken. The contributors reported earlier are Italy, France and Spain. No new official or unofficial Israeli reaction to the mission was found from Sunday evening to early Monday, in Hebrew or English media, in statements by the Foreign Ministry, the Prime Minister's Office or the IDF, or on X.

items.headline: Electricity Authority caps each new data center at 200 megawatts; reports differ on the national ceiling
items.lead: The plenum of Israel's Electricity Authority decided on Sunday evening, 18 October, that each new data center may connect to the grid at no more than 200 megawatts, and that developers must post guarantees of NIS 2 million per megawatt, or NIS 400 million for a full 200-megawatt site, to keep out speculative applications (Globes; TheMarker).
items.text: The plenum of Israel's Electricity Authority decided on Sunday evening, 18 October, that each new data center may connect to the grid at no more than 200 megawatts, and that developers must post guarantees of NIS 2 million per megawatt, or NIS 400 million for a full 200-megawatt site, to keep out speculative applications (Globes; TheMarker). The two papers differ on the total. Globes reports a ceiling of 1,300 megawatts for the whole sector, of which 300 megawatts must serve local users and the rest may serve foreign buyers of computing power. TheMarker reports a proposed ceiling of 3 gigawatts plus 300 megawatts reserved for the defense establishment, and says half of each guarantee would be returned only after 60 percent of the requested capacity is operating. TheMarker says the details had not yet been fully published, and the authority's own text was not found online, so the overall ceiling is unconfirmed. Other criteria, including a split between the center of the country and the periphery and preferences for developers who bring their own generation and storage, go to public comment; Globes expects the first new approvals to take at least several months, probably until after a new government is formed, and notes that more than one gigawatt of data centers was already approved under the earlier first-come policy. Requests submitted to the grid operator total about 27,000 megawatts, against a record peak demand of about 17,300 megawatts in August 2025; the freeze on new applications above 8 megawatts ends in early December (Bizportal).
